in_arabic.name: ميشاف
in_arabic.long_meaning: الميشاف هو اسم يعود إلى الجذر العربي 'م-ش-ف' والذي يعني الكتاب أو المصحف. في اللغة العربية، الميشاف هو المصحف الشريف أو كتاب الله الذي أنزل على النبي محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم. يشير الاسم إلى الحفاظ على كتاب الله ودراسته وتفسيره. في التاريخ الإسلامي، كان الميشاف رمزا للعلم والتوحيد.

in_urdu.name: میشاف
in_urdu.meaning: میشاف کا مطلب ہے کتاب یا مصحف
in_urdu.long_meaning: میشاف نام عربی جڑ 'م-ش-ف' سے نکلا ہے جس کا مطلب ہے کتاب یا مصحف۔ اردو میں، میشاف کو اللہ کی کتاب یا قرآن مجید کے طور پر سمجھا جاتا ہے جو حضرت محمد صلی اللہ علیہ وسلم پر نازل ہوا۔ یہ نام کتاب اللہ کے حفظ اور مطالعہ اور تفسير کی اہمیت کو ظاہر کرتا ہے۔ جنوبی ایشیائی مسلمانوں کے لئے، میشاف علم اور توحید کی علامت ہے۔

in_hindi.name: मिशाफ
in_hindi.meaning: मिशाफ का अर्थ है पुस्तक या कुरआन
in_hindi.long_meaning: मिशाफ नाम अरबी मूल 'म-श-फ' से आया है जिसका अर्थ है पुस्तक या कुरआन। हिंदी में, मिशाफ को अल्लाह की पुस्तक या कुरआन मजीद के रूप में समझा जाता है जो हज़रत मुहम्मद सल्लल्लाहु अलैहि वसल्लम पर उतारा गया। यह नाम अल्लाह की पुस्तक के संरक्षण और अध्ययन के महत्व को दर्शाता है। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में, मिशाफ ज्ञान और तौहीद का प्रतीक है।

in_pashto.name: ميشاف
in_pashto.meaning: ميشاف د کتاب يا قرآن معنی
in_pashto.long_meaning: ميشاف نوم د عربي ريښو 'م-ش-ف' څخه راځي چې د کتاب يا قرآن معنی ورکوي. په پښتو کې، ميشاف د الله کتاب يا قرآن مجيد ته اشاره کوي چې پر حضرت محمد صلی الله عليه وسلم باندې نازل شو. دا نوم د الله د کتاب د ساتنې او مطالعې اهميت ښيي. په افغان او پښتني دود کې، ميشاف د علم او توحيد نښه ده.

in_english.name: Mishaaf
in_english.meaning: Mishaaf means a book or a holy scripture
in_english.long_meaning: Mishaaf originates from the Arabic root 'm-sh-f', signifying a book or scripture. In Islamic context, Mishaaf refers to the Holy Quran or the scripture revealed to Prophet Muhammad. The name embodies the significance of preserving and studying the divine book. It symbolizes knowledge, unity, and spiritual growth in Islamic tradition. Historically, Mishaaf has been a term used to denote the sacred scripture across various Muslim cultures.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Mishaaf" carries a strong cultural significance in the Arab world, as it evokes images of courage, bravery, and strength. In various Arab literatures, including poetry and folklore, the lion is a powerful symbol representing fearlessness and valiance. Thus, bearing a name like Mishaaf means you are admired and respected for your brave and fearless demeanor, and expected to live up to these qualities in everyday life. It is a name that inspires confidence and trust, and instills a sense of pride in one's heritage and Arab identity.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Mishaaf" can be seen as a reminder of the inherent courage and strength that resides within every individual. It encourages us to confront our fears and challenges with bravery, knowing that we have the power to overcome them. Additionally, the name can serve as a source of inspiration and hope, reminding us that even in the darkest of times, we can find the strength to carry on and emerge victorious. Ultimately, the name Mishaaf reminds us of the divine power and strength that lies within us, and encourages us to live our lives in accordance with these noble qualities.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Maalik recorded in Al-Mawaaqit Wal-Duhaa that the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) sent an army led by Khalid ibn Al-Waleed to Mishaaf to confront the Byzantines under the command of Sa'd ibn Mu'aadh Al-Thaqafi. This battle took place during the early Caliphate of Umar ibn Al-Khattab (634-644 AD).

historical_references.context: Battle between Muslims and Byzantines at Mishaaf

historical_references.reference: Al-Baladhuri in Ansab Al-Ashraaf mentioned that during the reign of Caliph Umar ibn Abdul-Aziz (717-720 AD), a group of rebels led by Al-Ash'ath Al-Khuzaa'i took control of Damascus and were later repelled by Marwan ibn Muhammad. The rebels had taken refuge in Mishaaf, which was then a fortified place. Marwan besieged them and eventually captured Al-Ash'ath and ended the rebellion.
